script: John Walker's father died when he was 14 year old. The inheritance was just enough to buy a small grocery store in Kilmarnock, Scotland. Walker noticed that the whiskies he stocked tasted different every time a new batch arrived. Distilleries couldn't control the flavor from year to year, and customers kept complaining. So he started blending them himself, mixing barrels from different distilleries to create something consistent. It worked well enough that his whiskey outsold everything else in the store. His son Alexander expanded it into a proper brand, and his grandsons took it global. The square bottle was designed to fit more units in a shipping crate and reduce breakage, and the label was tilted at 24° so more text could fit on it. The Striding Man logo was sketched on a napkin during a business lunch in 1908 and never changed. None of it was designed by committee. Johnnie Walker is now the best-selling Scotch whisky in the world, sold in over 180 countries, and it started because a teenage boy needed to move inventory.
